cb_step_1.title: Select the pelvic CT scan
cb_step_1.simple: In the Input CT Volume box, choose the pelvic volume.
cb_step_1.detailed: This CT scan is the foundation for the entire plan: it provides the bone anatomy used to segment the pelvis and fracture fragments, generate reconstruction templates, guide reduction, and plan screw placement. Make sure the selected volume is the correct pelvic CT series before continuing.

cb_step_2.title: Run Step 1: Segment the pelvis
cb_step_2.simple: Click the 'Run Step 1: Segment Pelvis' button.
cb_step_2.detailed: This creates a 3D model of the intact pelvic bone, which will serve as the anatomical reference for reduction and fixation planning. Wait for the segmentation to finish before moving on.

cb_step_3.title: Center the 3D view
cb_step_3.simple: Click the Center view button in the 3D view.
cb_step_3.detailed: Centering the view gives you a clear overview of the pelvis and its fracture pattern. Rotate, zoom, or pan as needed so you can assess the anatomy before fracture segmentation.

cb_step_4.title: Run Step 2: Segment the fractures
cb_step_4.simple: Click the 'Run Step 2: Segment Fractures' button.
cb_step_4.detailed: This separates the fractured bone pieces from the intact pelvis so each fragment can be handled individually during reduction and fixation planning. Wait until the fracture fragments are complete before continuing.

cb_step_5.title: Merge small or insignificant fragments
cb_step_5.simple: In the untick section, uncheck each fracture segment that should be folded into a neighboring piece.
cb_step_5.detailed: Unchecking a fragment tells the software not to treat it as an independent piece, so it will be combined with an adjacent fragment instead. Use this for small or comminuted pieces that do not need individual repositioning, which simplifies the reduction plan.

cb_step_6.title: Decide whether a fragment needs manual splitting
cb_step_6.simple: Choose Yes if any remaining piece should be split manually, otherwise choose No.
cb_step_6.detailed: If automatic segmentation left a piece that actually contains two separate fragments that must move independently during reduction, you will split it manually. Otherwise, you can proceed directly toward template generation.

cb_step_7.title: Start manual separation
cb_step_7.detailed: This activates the manual cutting tool so you can divide a fused or incorrectly merged piece along a fracture line. The cutting plane you place next will determine how the piece is split.

cb_step_8.title: Place the cutting plane
cb_step_8.simple: In the 3D or slice views, place the cutting plane along the fracture line you want to split, then adjust its position and rotation.
cb_step_8.detailed: Align the plane so it follows the true fracture surface and cleanly divides the two fragments. The orientation of this plane is critical, because it determines exactly where and how the piece will be separated; then click Done.

cb_step_9.title: Confirm the separation
cb_step_9.detailed: This splits the selected piece using the cutting plane you placed. After confirmation, the software creates two separate fragments that can be repositioned independently during reduction.

cb_step_10.title: Run Step 3: Generate a template
cb_step_10.simple: Click the 'Run Step 3: Generate template' button.
cb_step_10.detailed: This creates a best-fit reconstruction template based on the segmented pelvis and fracture anatomy. The template will guide fracture reduction and subsequent implant planning, and can be manually adjusted in the next steps if needed.

cb_step_11.title: Decide whether to adjust the template
cb_step_11.simple: Choose Yes to tick 'Manually adjust a template', or No to skip manual adjustment.
cb_step_11.detailed: If the automatically generated template does not fit the patient's anatomy well enough, manual adjustment lets you fine-tune its position and rotation. If it already looks correct, you can proceed directly to the reduction step.

cb_step_12.title: Choose a template to adjust
cb_step_12.simple: In the Template selection box, choose the template you want to adjust.
cb_step_12.detailed: Selecting the correct template ensures your changes are applied to the intended reconstruction component. Adjust one template at a time; if another also needs changes, you will repeat this process.

cb_step_13.title: Review the template from a clear angle
cb_step_13.simple: Rotate, zoom, and pan the 3D view to see the selected template and its relationship to the pelvis.
cb_step_13.detailed: This view-only step helps you assess how the template sits against the pelvic bone before making any changes. Use a clear vantage point to judge the fit, then click Done when you are ready to proceed.

cb_step_14.title: Are there more templates to adjust?
cb_step_14.simple: Choose Yes if another template also needs adjustment, otherwise choose No.
cb_step_14.detailed: If more than one template requires fine-tuning, you can return to the selection step and adjust each one individually. Once all necessary templates have been handled, continue to apply the changes.

cb_step_15.title: Apply the template adjustments
cb_step_15.detailed: This finalizes the position and rotation changes you made to the selected templates and updates the reduction plan. The adjusted templates will be used in the next stage of the workflow.

cb_step_16.title: Run Step 4: Register and reduce the fracture
cb_step_16.detailed: This step aligns and reduces the fracture fragments toward the intact pelvis and template, producing a virtual reduction of the pelvic ring. The result creates the corrected bone alignment that will be used for screw planning.

cb_step_17.title: Decide whether to adjust fragments manually
cb_step_17.simple: Choose Yes to tick 'Manually adjust a fragment', or No to accept the automatic reduction.
cb_step_17.detailed: If a fragment is not perfectly reduced, manual adjustment lets you fine-tune its position and rotation to restore a more anatomical alignment. This is important before planning fixation across the fracture.

cb_step_18.title: Choose a fragment to adjust
cb_step_18.simple: In the Fragment selection box, choose the fragment you want to adjust.
cb_step_18.detailed: Selecting the correct fragment ensures your changes are applied to the intended bone piece. Adjust one fragment at a time; repeat this for any other fragments that need correction.

cb_step_19.title: Inspect the selected fragment from a good angle
cb_step_19.simple: Rotate, zoom, and pan the 3D view to inspect the selected fragment and its alignment.
cb_step_19.detailed: This view-only step lets you evaluate how the fragment sits relative to the rest of the reduced pelvis before making positional changes. Use a clear view to judge the alignment, then click Done when ready to continue.

cb_step_20.title: Are there more fragments to adjust?
cb_step_20.simple: Choose Yes if another fragment also needs adjustment, otherwise choose No.
cb_step_20.detailed: If several fragments were not perfectly reduced, you can return to the selection step and adjust each one individually. When the reduction looks acceptable, continue to apply the changes.

cb_step_21.title: Apply the fragment adjustments
cb_step_21.detailed: This finalizes the position and rotation changes for all adjusted fragments and updates the reduction. The corrected alignment is then used for planning screw trajectories.

cb_step_22.title: Run Step 5: Plan the screws
cb_step_22.simple: Click the 'Run Step 5: Plan Screws' button.
cb_step_22.detailed: This creates initial screw trajectories for fixing the reduced pelvis, based on the corrected bone alignment and template. Review these trajectories carefully, because they determine safe and effective implant placement.

cb_step_23.title: Decide whether to edit the screw trajectories
cb_step_23.simple: Choose Yes to tick 'Edit Screw trajectories', or No to finish the planning.
cb_step_23.detailed: If a planned screw trajectory is not safe or optimal, manual editing lets you relocate or reorient it to stay within bone and avoid critical structures. Otherwise, the current plan is final.

cb_step_24.title: Review the screw trajectories from a clear angle
cb_step_24.simple: Rotate, zoom, and pan the 3D view to examine the planned screw trajectories in relation to the bone.
cb_step_24.detailed: This view-only step helps you judge whether the trajectories are safely within bone and appropriately positioned for fixation. Make sure you can see each planned trajectory clearly, then click Done when ready to proceed.

cb_step_25.title: Regenerate screws from the edited lines
cb_step_25.simple: Click the 'Regenerate screws from edited lines' button.
cb_step_25.detailed: This rebuilds the final screw implants from your edited trajectories, replacing the automatically planned versions. Once regenerated, the screw plan reflects your clinical refinements.
